# Business Rules Checklist: Task Management Application

**Purpose**: Formal pre-implementation gate on the requirements quality of the three
constitution-critical business rules — duplicate detection, scheduling-conflict
detection, and drag-and-drop validation — before `/speckit-implement` begins.
**Created**: 2026-08-29
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Requirement Completeness

- [x] CHK001 Does the duplicate-detection requirement explicitly exclude a task from being flagged as a duplicate of *itself* during an update (not just the scheduling-conflict self-exception in FR-013)? [Gap, Spec §FR-009, FR-010, FR-013] — _Resolved: FR-010 now states a task is never compared against its own record on update._
- [x] CHK002 Is it specified whether the duplicate/scheduling-conflict checks consider deleted tasks (i.e., can a new task reuse the exact title+time or time slot of a task that was previously deleted)? [Gap, Spec §FR-005, FR-010, FR-011] — _Resolved: Edge Cases now states deletion is permanent and immediately frees the title/time for reuse._
- [x] CHK003 Is a requirement defined for what value `scheduled_at` takes when a task is dragged into the "unscheduled" grouping (cleared to null vs. retaining its last value)? [Gap, Spec §FR-006, FR-017] — _Resolved: Edge Cases now states it is cleared to unscheduled._
- [x] CHK004 Are requirements defined for the combined case where a single drag-and-drop move changes both status and schedule at once — does it state that both the duplicate check and the scheduling-conflict check must run against the new schedule regardless of the status change? [Completeness, Spec §FR-006, FR-008] — _Already satisfied: FR-008's "any change made via drag-and-drop" is unqualified, so a combined status+time move is not a special case — both checks always apply._
- [x] CHK005 Is a requirement defined for what the user sees while a drag-and-drop persistence request is pending (loading/in-flight state), distinct from the success and rejection states already defined? [Gap, Spec §User Story 4] — _Reviewer decision: intentionally left as an implementation detail. plan.md's optimistic-update pattern means the UI reflects the change immediately on drag, with no functionally required distinct pending state; no spec change needed._
- [x] CHK006 Are requirements defined for concurrent drag-and-drop operations by two sessions targeting the same time slot, or does the race-condition requirement only explicitly cover create requests? [Gap, Spec §Edge Cases] — _Resolved: the race-condition Edge Case now explicitly covers create, update, and drag-and-drop requests._

## Requirement Clarity

- [x] CHK007 Is the duplicate-detection title comparison rule specific enough to resolve titles that differ only in internal whitespace (e.g., single vs. double spaces between words), beyond the stated leading/trailing trim? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-010] — _Resolved: reviewer chose to collapse internal whitespace; FR-010 and data-model.md updated accordingly._
- [x] CHK008 Is "exact match, to the minute" for scheduling conflicts (FR-012) specific enough to state how sub-minute precision (seconds/milliseconds) supplied by a client is handled — truncated, rounded, or rejected? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-012] — _Resolved: FR-012 now specifies truncation (not rounding)._
- [x] CHK009 Does the spec clarify whether the duplicate/scheduling-conflict rules are case-sensitive or case-insensitive with respect to non-ASCII/Unicode title characters, or is "case-insensitive" only defined for the ASCII case? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-010] — _Resolved: FR-010 now states standard lowercase comparison is used and locale-specific case-folding is explicitly out of scope._
- [x] CHK010 Is the scope of "another task" in the scheduling-conflict rule (FR-011) explicit that it means *any* task regardless of status (including `done`), consistent with FR-018, everywhere the rule is stated? [Clarity, Spec §FR-011, FR-018] — _Already satisfied: FR-018 makes this globally true for every rule in the document, including FR-011._

## Requirement Consistency

- [x] CHK011 Are the duplicate-detection requirements in the Functional Requirements section (FR-009, FR-010) consistent with the Clarifications log entry and User Story 2's acceptance scenarios in their description of what counts as a match? [Consistency, Spec §Clarifications, FR-010] — _Verified consistent._
- [x] CHK012 Are the scheduling-conflict requirements consistent between User Story 2 (create/update) and User Story 4 (drag-and-drop) in how they describe the rejection message and the retained/reverted state? [Consistency, Spec §User Story 2, User Story 4] — _Verified consistent (the wording differs only because forms vs. drag are different interaction models, not because the underlying rule differs)._
- [x] CHK013 Is FR-018's "no status-based exemption" statement consistent with every other business-rule requirement (FR-007, FR-009, FR-010, FR-011) — i.e., none of them separately imply or allow a status-based carve-out? [Consistency, Spec §FR-007, FR-009, FR-010, FR-011, FR-018] — _Verified consistent: none of those FRs mention status at all, so FR-018's blanket statement doesn't conflict with anything._

## Drag-and-Drop Requirement Coverage

- [x] CHK014 Are requirements defined for every invalid drop destination category (occupied time slot, non-drop-target area), or only the occupied-time-slot case? [Coverage, Spec §FR-007, Edge Cases] — _Already satisfied: FR-007 covers the occupied-slot case and a separate Edge Case covers the non-drop-target case._
- [x] CHK015 Is a requirement defined for how the user is informed *which* rule (duplicate vs. scheduling conflict) rejected a drag-and-drop move, matching the same level of specificity required for create/update rejections (FR-016)? [Gap, Spec §FR-016, User Story 4] — _Already satisfied: FR-016 applies to "backend-returned errors" without scoping by operation type, and FR-008 ties drag to the same backend path, so the same duplicate/conflict specificity automatically carries over._
- [x] CHK016 Are requirements defined for what happens to a task's on-screen position if the backend request for a drag-and-drop move times out (as opposed to returning an explicit error response)? [Gap, Spec §Edge Cases] — _Already satisfied: User Story 4's acceptance scenario 4 ("fails for any reason") and the Edge Cases backend-unreachable bullet are both worded broadly enough to include timeouts._
- [x] CHK017 Is it explicit that a drag-and-drop move is validated through the exact same duplicate/conflict rule as a form-based edit, with no reduced or different validation for drag operations specifically? [Clarity, Spec §FR-008] — _Already satisfied: FR-008 states this directly._

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [x] CHK018 Can "100% of attempts... are rejected" (SC-002, SC-003) be objectively verified without additional detail on what constitutes the full population of "attempts" being measured? [Measurability, Spec §SC-002, SC-003] — _Resolved in practice: tasks.md's test suite (T023, T024, T026, T028, T029) enumerates the concrete attempt population — same-title+time, different-title+time, concurrent, update-created, and Done-status cases._
- [x] CHK019 Are the acceptance scenarios for User Story 2 sufficient to distinguish a test for the duplicate rule from a test for the scheduling-conflict rule, given that every duplicate is also a conflict (FR-010 is a subset of FR-011)? [Ambiguity, Spec §User Story 2, FR-010, FR-011] — _Resolved at the appropriate layer: research.md §3 documents that the duplicate check runs before the conflict check, so a title+time match always reports as a duplicate — the ordering decision correctly lives in plan/research, not the tech-agnostic spec._
- [x] CHK020 Is SC-006 ("leave the board in a consistent state") measurable independently of implementation, or does it require a more specific, verifiable definition of "consistent state" for drag-and-drop rejections? [Measurability, Spec §SC-006] — _Already satisfied: SC-006 already includes the concrete parenthetical "(the task visibly returns to its prior position)."_

## Dependencies & Assumptions

- [x] CHK021 Is the assumption that duplicate/scheduling-conflict detection operates globally across the single shared workspace (not scoped to any board/list subdivision) explicitly stated, given the spec defines no such subdivision? [Assumption, Spec §Assumptions] — _Already satisfied: the spec defines no board/list subdivision anywhere, so there is nothing for the rule to be ambiguously scoped against._
- [x] CHK022 Is the dependency between the scheduling-conflict rule and the duplicate rule (every duplicate necessarily also being a conflict, per FR-010/FR-011) called out anywhere in the requirements, so a reader understands why both rules are needed? [Gap, Spec §FR-010, FR-011] — _Resolved at the appropriate layer: research.md §3 explains this relationship and why both checks exist; this is an implementation-rationale note, not a user-facing requirement, so research.md is the correct home for it rather than spec.md._

## Ambiguities & Conflicts

- [x] CHK023 Does the spec resolve whether a task's `description` field participates in duplicate detection in any way, or is it explicitly and solely title + schedule (FR-010)? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-010, Key Entities] — _Already satisfied: FR-010 exhaustively enumerates title + scheduled date/time as the only comparison fields._
- [x] CHK024 Is there any remaining conflict between the original Input description ("Two tasks cannot have the same scheduled time") and the refined FR-012 definition (exact match to the minute, no duration), or has the Clarifications log fully superseded the original phrasing? [Conflict, Spec §Input, FR-012, Clarifications] — _Already satisfied: the Input field is preserved verbatim as historical record per standard practice, and the Clarifications log documents the full, final resolution that FR-012 encodes._
